newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish markets brace for interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish markets brace for interest rate rise.

text.p: Poland's money and foreign exchange markets are braced for the very real possiblility of an official interest rate rise in the near future, analysts said on F riday.

Although the analysts are far from agreed in their expectations, most see official interest rates rising roughly one or two percentage points to curb credit growth and offset the effects of extra central bank financing of flood relief.

"It seems the central bank will increase rates by one to two points...and do so quickly...to offset government demand for credit and set a new benchmark," said Krzysztof Bledowski, chief economist at WoodCommerz in Warsaw.

Late on Thursday National Bank of Poland president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said: "Real interest rates will keep on growing and we should forget for many months about rate cuts and there is a very real possibility of a nominal rate rise."
Analysts said the money market was already pricing in a nominal rate rise with one-month deposits quotes straddling the 25 percent lombard rate on Friday, up a point from Thursday.

"Higher market rates should be set at upcoming central bank open-market operations but players seem to already be assuming an official rise by offering one-month deposits above lombard," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.

Wieczorkiewicz added that the central bank may delay a nominal rate rise until it can better estimate the extent of damage suffered to southern Poland during a weeks-long flood, which weather forecasters said could worsen over the weekend.
Dealers said one-day rates may be volatile next week as banks fine-tune reserve requirements in the last full week of the monthly reseve, which ends on July 30.
Treasury-bill yields were expected to rise sharply at Monday's 1.1 billion zloty primary auction amid small demand from investors, seen totalling only about half a billion, dealers said.

The yield of the 52-week T-bill was seen capped at 22.25 percent versus this week's 22.00 as the finance ministry, now with a larger credit line with the NBP, may reject lower bids at levels even with Friday's secondary quotes at 22.63 percent.

The zloty, battered to all-time lows by speculative sales and foreign withdrawal this week, was expected to remain range-bound between central bank interventions foreign sell orders, despite expectations of a rise in official interest rates.
"Higher rates are a positive sign in theory, but recent interest rate moves have not had any significant effect on the zloty," said Bogdan Stempkowski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said however that an interest rate rise could open up the gates for currency speculators, especially if the central bank established a support level for the zloty.
The zloty ended the week around 3.3 percent below parity, up from all-time lows of 5.7 percent below parity on Tuesday but much below last week's close at 0.2 percent above parity.
